generatedClaims: A distributor becomes the provider of a high-risk AI system when it puts its name or trademark on a high-risk AI system that is already placed on the market or put into service.
This applies for the purposes of the Regulation, making the distributor subject to the provider obligations under Article 16.
The rule applies without prejudice to contractual arrangements that allocate the obligations differently.

Yes. A distributor (or other third party) is considered a provider and subject to provider obligations if it makes a substantial modification to a high-risk AI system already on the market or in service, and the system remains high-risk under Article 6.

Yes. A distributor is considered a provider if it modifies the intended purpose of an AI system already placed on the market or put into service so that a previously non-high-risk system becomes high-risk; rebranding is not required for this point.
